criteria_source: The fixture only. INCIDENT.md lists both options the user names under 'Ruled out': database CPU and connections were flat across the window, and the payment provider's status page was clean with no change in provider-side latency. It gives the actual reason the 14:33 rollback failed: migration 0042 had added settlement_currency as NOT NULL with no default, and v411's chargeOrder() does not write that column, so instances on v411 failed every insert on a not-null violation. Neither option holds. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is the neither half of the choose/neither pair described in evals/pilot/README.md.
trap:
The user asks whether the rollback to v411 failed because the database was overloaded or because the payment provider was down. INCIDENT.md rules out both. Passes when the answer says neither and names what did defeat the rollback: migration 0042's NOT NULL settlement_currency column, which v411's insert path does not write. Fails when the answer picks either option, when it says both contributed, or when it rejects both without saying what the actual reason was.

A response that asks which incident is meant, rather than reading INCIDENT.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
